title: Knocking on the Website
summary: Two visitors to the company website set off the same alarm: lots of 'page not found'. One is a search engine following old links. The other is trying doors.
story: You are the analyst on shift at {{CO}} (a made-up company). The website runs on WEB01, and the SIEM collects its visitor log: every page asked for, by which address, and whether it worked (status 200) or wasn't there (404). A rule fires when one visitor gets many 404s in a short time. It fired twice today.
goal: Decide which alert is real, find the address that was looking for weaknesses and the file it managed to download, when, and what its program called itself.
skills: reading web server logs, status codes, user agents, counting by field

questions.ask: The alert about the visitor {{QIP}}: real attack or false alarm? (one try)
questions.explain: {{BOTIP}} asked for robots.txt first, then followed old product links, and says it is a search engine's crawler: harmless. {{SCANIP}} asked for admin pages, settings files and backups that no visitor should want - a tool trying doors.

questions.ask: Which address was looking for weaknesses?
questions.explain: Its 404s are all well-known secret or admin paths.

questions.ask: Which file did it manage to download (its one request that worked)?
questions.explain: The only status=200 for that address.

questions.ask: At what time (HH:MM:SS) did it get that file?
questions.explain: The time of that status=200 request.

questions.ask: What did that visitor's program call itself (the agent field, the name before the /)?
questions.explain: agent= is what the visitor's program says it is. Tools can lie about it, but many don't bother.

hints.text: What to think about first: a 404 just means 'that page isn't here'. Ordinary visitors get a few from old links. The question is which pages a visitor asked for. Someone asking for /admin, /.env (a settings file) or /backup.zip is guessing where secrets might be; someone asking for old product pages is following links that used to work.

siem alerts shows the two alerts and the client= address each is about. To see one visitor's requests: siem search source=web client=ADDRESS. Each line shows the path= asked for, the status= (200 worked, 404 not found) and the agent= (what the visitor's program says it is).

siem search source=web client=ADDRESS --count-by status counts how many requests got each status. For the address that was guessing, one request worked: siem search source=web client=ADDRESS status=200 shows which file it downloaded, and its time= is when.

A search engine's crawler usually asks for /robots.txt first (the file where websites tell robots what they may visit) and names itself with a web address in its agent. The other visitor's agent names a scanning tool. Answer real for the scanner's alert and false alarm for the crawler's.
